The Mermaid code defines how nodes and edges are made and accommodates different arrow types, multi-directional arrows, and any linking to and from subgraphs.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;warning\nIf you are using the word \"end\" in a Flowchart node, capitalize the entire word or any of the letters (e.g., \"End\" or \"END\"), or apply this [workaround](https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/issues/1444#issuecomment-639528897). It renders in the same way as &#96;A[\"A\"]&#96;, or &#96;A&#96;.\n\nAdditionally, you can specify a &#96;label&#96; this way, which allows you to escape characters that the normal Mermaid syntax does Rectangle)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nflowchart TD\n  %% aliases: tagged-process, tag-proc, tagged-rectangle\n  A@{ shape: tag-rect, label: \"Tagged process\" }\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Special shapes in Mermaid Flowcharts (v11.3.0+)\n\nMermaid also introduces 2 special shapes to enhance your flowcharts: **icon** and **image**. These shapes allow you to include icons and images directly within your flowcharts, providing more visual context and clarity.\n\n### Icon Shape\n\nYou can use the &#96;icon&#96; shape to include an icon in your flowchart. To use icons, you need to register the icon pack first. Follow the instructions provided [here](../config/icons.md). The syntax for defining an icon shape is as follows:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nflowchart TD\n    A@{ icon: \"fa:user\", form: \"square\", label: \"User Icon\", pos: \"t\", h: 60 }\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Parameters\n\n- **icon**: The name of the icon from the registered icon pack.\n- **form**: Specifies the background shape of the icon. If not defined there will be no background to icon. Options include:\n  - &#96;square&#96;\n  - &#96;circle&#96;\n  - &#96;rounded&#96;\n- **label**: The text label associated with the icon. This can be any string. If not defined, no label will be displayed.\n- **pos**: The position of the label. If not defined label will default to bottom of icon. Possible values are:\n  - &#96;t&#96;\n  - &#96;b&#96;\n- **h**: The height of the icon. If not defined this will default to 48 which is minimum.\n\n### Image Shape\n\nYou can use the &#96;image&#96; shape to include an image in your flowchart. The syntax for defining an image shape is as follows:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nflowchart TD\n    A@{ img: \"https://example.com/image.png\", label: \"Image Label\", pos: \"t\", w: 60, h: 60, constraint: \"off\" }\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Parameters\n\n- **img**: The URL of the image to be displayed.\n- **label**: The text label associated with the image. This can be any string. If not defined, no label will be displayed.\n- **pos**: The position of the label. If not defined, the label will default to the bottom of the image. Possible values are:\n  - &#96;t&#96;\n  - &#96;b&#96;\n- **w**: The width of the image. If not defined, this will default to the natural width of the image.\n- **h**: The height of the image. If not defined, this will default to the natural height of the image.\n- **constraint**: Determines if the image should constrain the node size. This setting also ensures the image maintains its original aspect ratio, adjusting the width (&#96;w&#96;) accordingly to the height (&#96;h&#96;). If not defined, this will default to &#96;off&#96; Possible values are:\n  - &#96;on&#96;\n  - &#96;off&#96;\n\nIf you want to resize an image, but keep the same aspect ratio, set &#96;h&#96;, and set &#96;constraint: on&#96; to constrain the aspect ratio. E.g.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nflowchart TD\n  %% My image with a constrained aspect ratio\n  A@{ img: \"https://mermaid.js.org/favicon.svg\", label: \"My example image label\", pos: \"t\", h: 60, constraint: \"on\" }\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Links between nodes\n\nNodes can be connected with links/edges. It is possible to have different types of links or attach a text string to a link.\n\n### A link with arrow head\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nflowchart LR\n    A--&gt;B\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### An open link\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nflowchart LR\n    A --- B\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Text on links\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nflowchart LR\n    A-- This is the text! ---B\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nor\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nflowchart LR\n    A---|This is the text|B\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### A link with arrow head and text\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nflowchart LR\n    A--&gt;|text|B\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nor\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nflowchart LR\n    A-- text --&gt;B\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Dotted link\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nflowchart LR\n   A-.-&gt;B;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Dotted link with text\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nflowchart LR\n   A-. text .-&gt; B\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Thick link\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nflowchart LR\n   A ==&gt; B\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Thick link with text\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nflowchart LR\n   A == text ==&gt; B\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### An invisible link\n\nThis can be a useful tool in some instances where you want to alter the default positioning of a node.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nflowchart LR\n    A ~~~ B\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Chaining of links\n\nIt is possible declare many links in the same line as per below:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nflowchart LR\n   A -- text --&gt; B -- text2 --&gt; C\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nIt is also possible to declare multiple nodes links in the same line as per below:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nflowchart LR\n   a --&gt; b &amp; c--&gt; d\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nYou can then describe dependencies in a very expressive way. Like the one-liner below:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nflowchart TB\n    A &amp; B--&gt; C &amp; D\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nIf you describe the same diagram using the basic syntax, it will take four lines. A\nword of warning, one could go overboard with this making the flowchart harder to read in\nmarkdown form. The Swedish word &#96;lagom&#96; comes to mind. It means, not too much and not too little.\nThis goes for expressive syntaxes as well.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nflowchart TB\n    A --&gt; C\n    A --&gt; D\n    B --&gt; C\n    B --&gt; D\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Attaching an ID to Edges\n\nMermaid now supports assigning IDs to edges, similar to how IDs and metadata can be attached to nodes. This feature lays the groundwork for more advanced styling, classes, and animation capabilities on edges.\n\n**Syntax:**\n\nTo give an edge an ID, prepend the edge syntax with the ID followed by an &#96;@&#96; character. For example:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nflowchart LR\n  A e1@–&gt; B\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nIn this example, &#96;e1&#96; is the ID of the edge connecting &#96;A&#96; to &#96;B&#96;. You can then use this ID in later definitions or style statements, just like with nodes.\n\n### Turning an Animation On\n\nOnce you have assigned an ID to an edge, you can turn on animations for that edge by defining the edge’s properties:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nflowchart LR\n  A e1@==&gt; B\n  e1@{ animate: true }\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThis tells Mermaid that the edge &#96;e1&#96; should be animated.\n\n### Selecting Type of Animation\n\nIn the initial version, two animation speeds are supported: &#96;fast&#96; and &#96;slow&#96;. Selecting a specific animation type is a shorthand for enabling animation and setting the animation speed in one go.\n\n**Examples:**\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nflowchart LR\n  A e1@–&gt; B\n  e1@{ animation: fast }\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThis is equivalent to &#96;{ animate: true, animation: fast }&#96;.\n\n### Using classDef Statements for Animations\n\nYou can also animate edges by assigning a class to them and then defining animation properties in a &#96;classDef&#96; statement. For example:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nflowchart LR\n  A e1@–&gt; B\n  classDef animate stroke-dasharray: 9,5,stroke-dashoffset: 900,animation: dash 25s linear infinite;\n  class e1 animate\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nIn this snippet:\n\n- &#96;e1@--&gt;&#96; creates an edge with ID &#96;e1&#96;.\n- &#96;classDef animate&#96; defines a class named &#96;animate&#96; with styling and animation properties.\n- &#96;class e1 animate&#96; applies the &#96;animate&#96; class to the edge &#96;e1&#96;.\n\n**Note on Escaping Commas:**\nWhen setting the &#96;stroke-dasharray&#96; property, remember to escape commas as &#96;\\,&#96; since commas are used as delimiters in Mermaid’s style definitions.\n\n## New arrow types\n\nThere are new types of arrows supported:\n\n- circle edge\n- cross edge\n\n### Circle edge example\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nflowchart LR\n    A --o B\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Cross edge example\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nflowchart LR\n    A --x B\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Multi directional arrows\n\nThere is the possibility to use multidirectional arrows.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nflowchart LR\n    A o--o B\n    B &lt;--&gt; C\n    C x--x D\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Minimum length of a link\n\nEach node in the flowchart is ultimately assigned to a rank in the rendered\ngraph, i.e. to a vertical or horizontal level (depending on the flowchart\norientation), based on the nodes to which it is linked. By default, links\ncan span any number of ranks, but you can ask for any link to be longer\nthan the others by adding extra dashes in the link definition.\n\nIn the following example, two extra dashes are added in the link from node _B_\nto node _E_, so that it spans two more ranks than regular links:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nflowchart TD\n    A[\"Start\"] --&gt; B{\"Is it?\"}\n    B --&gt;|Yes| C[\"OK\"]\n    C --&gt; D[\"Rethink\"]\n    D --&gt; B\n    B ----&gt;|No| E[\"End\"]\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&gt; **Note** Links may still be made longer than the requested number of ranks\n&gt; by the rendering engine to accommodate other requests.\n\nWhen the link label is written in the middle of the link, the extra dashes must\nbe added on the right side of the link. The following example is equivalent to\nthe previous one:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nflowchart TD\n    A[\"Start\"] --&gt; B{\"Is it?\"}\n    B -- Yes --&gt; C[\"OK\"]\n    C --&gt; D[\"Rethink\"]\n    D --&gt; B\n    B -- No ----&gt; E[\"End\"]\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nFor dotted or thick links, the characters to add are equals signs or dots,\nas summed up in the following table:\n\n| Length            |   1    |    2    |    3     |\n| ----------------- | :----: | :-----: | :------: |\n| Normal            | &#96;---&#96;  | &#96;----&#96;  | &#96;-----&#96;  |\n| Normal with arrow | &#96;--&gt;&#96;  | &#96;---&gt;&#96;  | &#96;----&gt;&#96;  |\n| Thick             | &#96;===&#96;  | &#96;====&#96;  | &#96;=====&#96;  |\n| Thick with arrow  | &#96;==&gt;&#96;  | &#96;===&gt;&#96;  | &#96;====&gt;&#96;  |\n| Dotted            | &#96;-.-&#96;  | &#96;-..-&#96;  | &#96;-...-&#96;  |\n| Dotted with arrow | &#96;-.-&gt;&#96; | &#96;-..-&gt;&#96; | &#96;-...-&gt;&#96; |\n\n## Special characters that break syntax\n\nIt is possible to put text within quotes in order to render more troublesome characters. As in the example below:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nflowchart LR\n    id1[\"This is the (text) in the box\"]\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Entity codes to escape characters\n\nIt is possible to escape characters using the syntax exemplified here.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\n    flowchart LR\n        A[\"A double quote:#quot;\"] --&gt; B[\"A dec char:#9829;\"]\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nNumbers given are base 10, so &#96;#&#96; can be encoded as &#96;#35;&#96;. It is also supported to use HTML character names.\n\n## Subgraphs\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nsubgraph title\n    graph definition\nend\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nAn example below:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nflowchart TB\n    c1--&gt;a2\n    subgraph one\n    a1--&gt;a2\n    end\n    subgraph two\n    b1--&gt;b2\n    end\n    subgraph three\n    c1--&gt;c2\n    end\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nYou can also set an explicit id for the subgraph.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nflowchart TB\n    c1--&gt;a2\n    subgraph ide1 [\"one\"]\n    a1--&gt;a2\n    end\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### flowcharts\n\nWith the graphtype flowchart it is also possible to set edges to and from subgraphs as in the flowchart below.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nflowchart TB\n    c1--&gt;a2\n    subgraph one\n    a1--&gt;a2\n    end\n    subgraph two\n    b1--&gt;b2\n    end\n    subgraph three\n    c1--&gt;c2\n    end\n    one --&gt; two\n    three --&gt; two\n    two --&gt; c2\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Direction in subgraphs\n\nWith the graphtype flowcharts you can use the direction statement to set the direction which the subgraph will render like in this example.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nflowchart LR\n  subgraph TOP\n    direction TB\n    subgraph B1\n        direction RL\n        i1 --&gt;f1\n    end\n    subgraph B2\n        direction BT\n        i2 --&gt;f2\n    end\n  end\n  A --&gt; TOP --&gt; B\n  B1 --&gt; B2\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### Limitation\n\nIf any of a subgraph's nodes are linked to the outside, subgraph direction will be ignored. Instead the subgraph will inherit the direction of the parent graph:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nflowchart LR\n    subgraph subgraph1\n        direction TB\n        top1[\"top\"] --&gt; bottom1[\"bottom\"]\n    end\n    subgraph subgraph2\n        direction TB\n        top2[\"top\"] --&gt; bottom2[\"bottom\"]\n    end\n    %% ^ These subgraphs are identical, except for the links to them:\n\n    %% Link *to* subgraph1: subgraph1 direction is maintained\n    outside --&gt; subgraph1\n    %% Link *within* subgraph2:\n    %% subgraph2 inherits the direction of the top-level graph (LR)\n    outside ---&gt; top2\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Markdown Strings\n\nThe \"Markdown Strings\" feature enhances flowcharts and mind maps by offering a more versatile string type, which supports text formatting options such as bold and italics, and automatically wraps text within labels.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\n%%{init: {\"flowchart\": {\"htmlLabels\": false}} }%%\nflowchart LR\nsubgraph \"One\"\n  a(\"&#96;The **cat**\n  in the hat&#96;\") -- \"edge label\" --&gt; b{{\"&#96;The **dog** in the hog&#96;\"}}\nend\nsubgraph \"&#96;**Two**&#96;\"\n  c(\"&#96;The **cat**\n  in the hat&#96;\") -- \"&#96;Bold **edge label**&#96;\" --&gt; d(\"The dog in the hog\")\nend\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nFormatting:\n\n- For bold text, use double asterisks (&#96;**&#96;) before and after the text.\n- For italics, use single asterisks (&#96;*&#96;) before and after the text.\n- With traditional strings, you needed to add &#96;&lt;br&gt;&#96; tags for text to wrap in nodes. However, markdown strings automatically wrap text when it becomes too long and allows you to start a new line by simply using a newline character instead of a &#96;&lt;br&gt;&#96; tag.\n\nThis feature is applicable to node labels, edge labels, and subgraph labels.\n\nThe auto wrapping can be disabled by using\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n---\nconfig:\n  markdownAutoWrap: false\n---\ngraph LR\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Interaction\n\nIt is possible to bind a click event to a node, the click can lead to either a javascript callback or to a link which will be opened in a new browser tab.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;note\nThis functionality is disabled when using &#96;securityLevel='strict'&#96; and enabled when using &#96;securityLevel='loose'&#96;.\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nclick nodeId callback\nclick nodeId call callback()\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n- nodeId is the id of the node\n- callback is the name of a javascript function defined on the page displaying the graph, the function will be called with the nodeId as parameter.\n\nExamples of tooltip usage below:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;html\n&lt;script&gt;\n  window.callback = function () {\n    alert('A callback was triggered');\n  };\n&lt;/script&gt;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThe tooltip text is surrounded in double quotes. The styles of the tooltip are set by the class &#96;.mermaidTooltip&#96;.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nflowchart LR\n    A--&gt;B\n    B--&gt;C\n    C--&gt;D\n    click A callback \"Tooltip for a callback\"\n    click B \"https://www.github.com\" \"This is a tooltip for a link\"\n    click C call callback() \"Tooltip for a callback\"\n    click D href \"https://www.github.com\" \"This is a tooltip for a link\"\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&gt; **Success** The tooltip functionality and the ability to link to urls are available from version 0.5.2.\n\n?&gt; Due to limitations with how Docsify handles JavaScript callback functions, an alternate working demo for the above code can be viewed at [this jsfiddle](https://jsfiddle.net/yk4h7qou/2/).\n\nLinks are opened in the same browser tab/window by default. It is possible to change this by adding a link target to the click definition (&#96;_self&#96;, &#96;_blank&#96;, &#96;_parent&#96; and &#96;_top&#96; are supported):\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nflowchart LR\n    A--&gt;B\n    B--&gt;C\n    C--&gt;D\n    D--&gt;E\n    click A \"https://www.github.com\" _blank\n    click B \"https://www.github.com\" \"Open this in a new tab\" _blank\n    click C href \"https://www.github.com\" _blank\n    click D href \"https://www.github.com\" \"Open this in a new tab\" _blank\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nBeginner's tip—a full example using interactive links in a html context:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;html\n&lt;body&gt;\n  &lt;pre class=\"mermaid\"&gt;\n    flowchart LR\n        A--&gt;B\n        B--&gt;C\n        C--&gt;D\n        click A callback \"Tooltip\"\n        click B \"https://www.github.com\" \"This is a link\"\n        click C call callback() \"Tooltip\"\n        click D href \"https://www.github.com\" \"This is a link\"\n  &lt;/pre&gt;\n\n  &lt;script&gt;\n    window.callback = function () {\n      alert('A callback was triggered');\n    };\n    const config = {\n      startOnLoad: true,\n      flowchart: { useMaxWidth: true, htmlLabels: true, curve: 'cardinal' },\n      securityLevel: 'loose',\n    };\n    mermaid.initialize(config);\n  &lt;/script&gt;\n&lt;/body&gt;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Comments\n\nComments can be entered within a flow diagram, which will be ignored by the parser. Comments need to be on their own line, and must be prefaced with &#96;%%&#96; (double percent signs). Any text after the start of the comment to the next newline will be treated as a comment, including any flow syntax\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nflowchart LR\n%% this is a comment A -- text --&gt; B{node}\n   A -- text --&gt; B -- text2 --&gt; C\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Styling and classes\n\n### Styling links\n\nIt is possible to style links. For instance, you might want to style a link that is going backwards in the flow. As links\nhave no ids in the same way as nodes, some other way of deciding what style the links should be attached to is required.\nInstead of ids, the order number of when the link was defined in the graph is used, or use default to apply to all links.\nIn the example below the style defined in the linkStyle statement will belong to the fourth link in the graph:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nlinkStyle 3 stroke:#ff3,stroke-width:4px,color:red;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nIt is also possible to add style to multiple links in a single statement, by separating link numbers with commas:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nlinkStyle 1,2,7 color:blue;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Styling line curves\n\nIt is possible to style the type of curve used for lines between items, if the default method does not meet your needs.\nAvailable curve styles include &#96;basis&#96;, &#96;bumpX&#96;, &#96;bumpY&#96;, &#96;cardinal&#96;, &#96;catmullRom&#96;, &#96;linear&#96;, &#96;monotoneX&#96;, &#96;monotoneY&#96;,\n&#96;natural&#96;, &#96;step&#96;, &#96;stepAfter&#96;, and &#96;stepBefore&#96;.\n\nIn this example, a left-to-right graph uses the &#96;stepBefore&#96; curve style:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n%%{ init: { 'flowchart': { 'curve': 'stepBefore' } } }%%\ngraph LR\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nFor a full list of available curves, including an explanation of custom curves, refer to\nthe [Shapes](https://d3js.org/d3-shape/curve) documentation in the [d3-shape](https://github.com/d3/d3-shape/) project.\n\n### Styling a node\n\nIt is possible to apply specific styles such as a thicker border or a different background color to a node.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nflowchart LR\n    id1(\"Start\")--&gt;id2(\"Stop\")\n    style id1 fill:#f9f,stroke:#333,stroke-width:4px\n    style id2 fill:#bbf,stroke:#f66,stroke-width:2px,color:#fff,stroke-dasharray: 5 5\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### Classes\n\nMore convenient than defining the style every time is to define a class of styles and attach this class to the nodes that\nshould have a different look.\n\nA class definition looks like the example below:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n    classDef className fill:#f9f,stroke:#333,stroke-width:4px;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nAlso, it is possible to define style to multiple classes in one statement:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n    classDef firstClassName,secondClassName font-size:12pt;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nAttachment of a class to a node is done as per below:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n    class nodeId1 className;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nIt is also possible to attach a class to a list of nodes in one statement:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n    class nodeId1,nodeId2 className;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nA shorter form of adding a class is to attach the classname to the node using the &#96;:::&#96;operator as per below:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nflowchart LR\n    A:::someclass --&gt; B\n    classDef someclass fill:#f96\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThis form can be used when declaring multiple links between nodes:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nflowchart LR\n    A:::foo &amp; B:::bar --&gt; C:::foobar\n    classDef foo stroke:#f00\n    classDef bar stroke:#0f0\n    classDef foobar stroke:#00f\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### CSS classes\n\nIt is also possible to predefine classes in CSS styles that can be applied from the graph definition as in the example\nbelow:\n\n**Example style**\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;html\n&lt;style&gt;\n  .cssClass &gt; rect {\n    fill: #ff0000;\n    stroke: #ffff00;\n    stroke-width: 4px;\n  }\n&lt;/style&gt;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Example definition**\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nflowchart LR\n    A--&gt;B[\"AAA&lt;span&gt;BBB&lt;/span&gt;\"]\n    B--&gt;D\n    class A cssClass\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Default class\n\nIf a class is named default it will be assigned to all classes without specific class definitions.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n    classDef default fill:#f9f,stroke:#333,stroke-width:4px;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Basic support for fontawesome\n\nIt is possible to add icons from fontawesome.\n\nThe icons are accessed via the syntax fa:#icon class name#.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nflowchart TD\n    B[\"fa:fa-twitter for peace\"]\n    B--&gt;C[\"fa:fa-ban forbidden\"]\n    B--&gt;D(\"fa:fa-spinner\")\n    B--&gt;E(\"A fa:fa-camera-retro perhaps?\")\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nMermaid supports Font Awesome if the CSS is included on the website.\nMermaid does not have any restriction on the version of Font Awesome that can be used.\n\nPlease refer the [Official Font Awesome Documentation](https://fontawesome.com/start) on how to include it in your website.\n\nAdding this snippet in the &#96;&lt;head&gt;&#96; would add support for Font Awesome v6.5.1\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;html\n&lt;link\n  href=\"https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/font-awesome/6.5.1/css/all.min.css\"\n  rel=\"stylesheet\"\n/&gt;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Custom icons\n\nIt is possible to use custom icons served from Font Awesome as long as the website imports the corresponding kit.\n\nNote that this is currently a paid feature from Font Awesome.\n\nFor custom icons, you need to use the &#96;fak&#96; prefix.\n\n**Example**\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nflowchart TD\n    B[\"fa:fa-twitter\"] %% standard icon\n    B--&gt;E(\"fak:fa-custom-icon-name\") %% custom icon\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nAnd trying to render it\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nflowchart TD\n    B[\"fa:fa-twitter for peace\"]\n    B--&gt;C[\"fab:fa-truck-bold a custom icon\"]\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Graph declarations with spaces between vertices and link and without semicolon\n\n- In graph declarations, the statements also can now end without a semicolon. After release 0.2.16, ending a graph statement with semicolon is just optional. So the below graph declaration is also valid along with the old declarations of the graph.\n\n- A single space is allowed between vertices and the link. However there should not be any space between a vertex and its text and a link and its text. The old syntax of graph declaration will also work and hence this new feature is optional and is introduced to improve readability.\n\nBelow is the new declaration of the graph edges which is also valid along with the old declaration of the graph edges.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nflowchart LR\n    A[\"Hard edge\"] --&gt;|Link text| B(\"Round edge\")\n    B --&gt; C{\"Decision\"}\n    C --&gt;|One| D[\"Result one\"]\n    C --&gt;|Two| E[\"Result two\"]\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Common Issues\n\n- &#96;end&#96; is a keyword in Mermaid flowcharts, so **NEVER** use it as a Node ID.\n- Always quote labels with &#96;\"&#96; to support special characters like parentheses in labels e.g.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nflowchart TD\n  %% Without the &#96;[\"&#96; &#96;\"]&#96;, this would be a syntax error\n  nodeID[\"This label supports (){}[]\"]\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n- Never use &#96;\"&#96; in a node label. If you need to use it, the only way it's supported is by escaping it with &#96;&amp;quot;&#96;, e.g.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nflowchart TD\n  nodeID[\"He said: &amp;quot;Hello World&amp;quot;\"]\n  pressButton[\"Press the &amp;quot;Start&amp;quot; button\"]\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n- Comments with &#96;%%&#96; must be on their own line\n\n&lt;!--- cspell:ignore lagom ---&gt;\n"
      }
    ]
  },
  "isConfirmed": {
    "type": 1
  },
  "content": "",
  "textEditContent": "",
  "toolCallResult": null
}

{
  "invocationMessage": "正在建立 [](file:///Users/xjp/Desktop/Survey-with-LLMs/Survey-for-survey-review-with-LLMs/SurveyX/my_docs/attribute_tree_flowchart.md)",
  "pastTenseMessage": "已建立 [](file:///Users/xjp/Desktop/Survey-with-LLMs/Survey-for-survey-review-with-LLMs/SurveyX/my_docs/attribute_tree_flowchart.md)",

  "textEditContent": "# AttributeTree 構建流程圖（投影片版本）\n\n&gt; 以下提供多種可用於投影片的 Mermaid 流程圖版本\n\n---\n\n## 版本 1：完整流程圖（垂直佈局）\n\n適合展示整體架構的詳細流程。\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\n%%{init: {'theme': 'base', 'themeVariables': { 'primaryColor': '#e3f2fd', 'primaryTextColor': '#1565c0', 'primaryBorderColor': '#1565c0', 'lineColor': '#42a5f5', 'secondaryColor': '#fff3e0', 'tertiaryColor': '#ffffff', 'fontSize': '16px'}}}%%\nflowchart TB\n    subgraph INPUT[\"📥 輸入階段\"]\n        A[\"📄 PDF 論文集合\"]\n        B[\"📝 Markdown 轉換&lt;br/&gt;(Docling)\"]\n    end\n    \n    subgraph STEP1[\"🏷️ Step 1: 論文分類\"]\n        C[\"📋 讀取 Abstract\"]\n        D{\"🤖 LLM 分類\"}\n        E1[\"Method&lt;br/&gt;方法類\"]\n        E2[\"Benchmark&lt;br/&gt;基準類\"]\n        E3[\"Theory&lt;br/&gt;理論類\"]\n        E4[\"Survey&lt;br/&gt;綜述類\"]\n    end\n    \n    subgraph STEP2[\"🌳 Step 2: AttributeTree 提取\"]\n        F1[\"attri_tree_for_method.md\"]\n        F2[\"attri_tree_for_benchmark.md\"]\n        F3[\"attri_tree_for_theory.md\"]\n        F4[\"attri_tree_for_survey.md\"]\n        G[\"🤖 LLM 結構化提取\"]\n    end\n    \n    subgraph OUTPUT[\"📤 輸出階段\"]\n        H[\"📊 JSON 結構化資料\"]\n        I[\"🌲 Attribute Forest&lt;br/&gt;屬性森林\"]\n    end\n    \n    A --&gt; B\n    B --&gt; C\n    C --&gt; D\n    D --&gt; E1 &amp; E2 &amp; E3 &amp; E4\n    E1 --&gt; F1\n    E2 --&gt; F2\n    E3 --&gt; F3\n    E4 --&gt; F4\n    F1 &amp; F2 &amp; F3 &amp; F4 --&gt; G\n    G --&gt; H\n    H --&gt; I\n\n    style A fill:#bbdefb,stroke:#1565c0,stroke-width:2px\n    style B fill:#bbdefb,stroke:#1565c0,stroke-width:2px\n    style D fill:#fff9c4,stroke:#f9a825,stroke-width:2px\n    style G fill:#fff9c4,stroke:#f9a825,stroke-width:2px\n    style H fill:#c8e6c9,stroke:#388e3c,stroke-width:2px\n    style I fill:#c8e6c9,stroke:#388e3c,stroke-width:2px\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## 版本 2：簡化版水平流程圖\n\n適合快速概覽，放在投影片上較為簡潔。\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\n%%{init: {'theme': 'base', 'themeVariables': { 'primaryColor': '#e8f5e9', 'primaryTextColor': '#2e7d32', 'primaryBorderColor': '#43a047', 'lineColor': '#66bb6a', 'secondaryColor': '#fffde7', 'tertiaryColor': '#ffffff', 'fontSize': '14px'}}}%%\nflowchart LR\n    A[\"📄 PDF&lt;br/&gt;論文\"] --&gt;
